content.text: In a harbour city where the tide returns lost objects, apprentice cartographer Sora finds an atlas that records days nobody remembers living. Each map belongs to a stranger; every borrowed day must eventually be returned.

Following the margins from a night market to an observatory built beneath the sea, Sora meets a retired translator, a girl who writes letters to her future self, and a ferryman who has forgotten his own name. Their separate stories form a quietly intricate novel about friendship, migration and the work of remembering.

The book alternates its central journey with fifteen short interludes, each written in a different voice. Leila Haddad’s original map illustrations are part of the work; translated editions retain their own publication and translation credits.

The closing movement returns to the harbour during the festival of low water. Small choices from the opening chapters acquire new meanings, while the city’s many languages remain deliberately visible.
An atlas cannot tell you where to belong. It can only show who travelled beside you.
